description: Polish pass on the shipped chat-v1 build, from the A–G QA walkthrough. Six substantive UX refinements on top of the existing chat surfaces (trivial fixes already landed by hand). Mostly UI wiring against contracts the chat-v1 loop already built. Source: docs/chat-v1-qa-backlog.md + prd-conan-chat-v1-polish.md. Runs on the loop/conan-chat-v1 git branch; the completed 25-story chat-v1 prd.json is archived under archive/2026-07-23-conan-chat-v1-complete/.

userStories.title: Unlock the permission mode chip — change mode mid-conversation
userStories.description: As a user, I want to change the permission mode (Supervised / Accept edits / Full access / Plan) at any point in a conversation, not just before the first turn — model and cwd stay locked, but the mode should be live-switchable.
acceptanceCriteria: The composer's PERMISSION chip is NOT locked after the first turn (the model chip + cwd pill stay locked as today — one process = one model/dir)
Before the first turn: selecting a mode sets the local launch state (unchanged)

After the first turn (live session): selecting a mode calls useAgentChat.setPermissionMode(mode) — the existing US-022 control-request switch — and the chip reflects the live `permissionMode` reported by the hook
The Full-access one-time confirm dialog still gates selecting bypassPermissions, live too; declining reverts
A failed live switch surfaces honestly (the hook already emits an error item) and the chip stays on the prior mode
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes

Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: send a turn, then switch the mode via the chip and confirm the change takes effect (e.g. Supervised→Full access: a subsequent tool no longer raises the approval panel)
userStories.notes: Backend already supports it (setPermissionMode, US-022) — this is UI wiring in ChatPane.tsx. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Auto-open the most recent thread on load
userStories.description: As a user, when I open the app I want my most recent conversation to reopen automatically instead of landing on 'No open chats' — so persistence feels real rather than looking like everything cleared.
acceptanceCriteria: On boot, after the persisted projects/threads load (GET /api/agent/projects), if at least one saved thread exists and nothing is open, auto-open (reopen — the US-015 flow) the thread with the newest last_activity
The auto-opened thread reconstructs its transcript from JSONL and can be continued via --resume, exactly as a manual reopen does
If NO saved threads exist, keep the current behavior (a fresh draft thread)
After the user EXPLICITLY closes a thread down to none in a session, show 'No open chats' — do not immediately re-auto-open (only auto-open on a fresh load)
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: with a saved thread present, reload the app and confirm it opens automatically showing restored history (not the empty state)
userStories.notes: Frontend in ChatSurface.tsx boot logic; reuses the US-015 reopen path. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: In-UI Settings + theme entry point
userStories.description: As a user, I want a visible way to reach Settings (theme, license) from the chat UI — right now it only opens from the native menu, so themes are unreachable in the browser and buried in the app.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a Settings affordance (gear icon) to the sidebar — bottom of the rail, standard chat-app placement — that dispatches the existing `conan:open-settings` window event and opens SettingsView
Add a direct ⌘, / Ctrl+, keyboard handler at the app level (not only via the native menu) so Settings is reachable without Tauri; must not fire while typing in the composer/inputs
SettingsView is reachable to the Appearance tab (Light/Dark/Auto theme switch works and reskins the app) AND the License tab
The gear is reachable in both expanded and collapsed sidebar states (or the keyboard shortcut covers collapsed)
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: click the gear → Settings opens → switch to Dark → the app goes dark
userStories.notes: SettingsView + useThemes already exist; this adds the missing entry points. The native menu path stays. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Stronger skill-tick treatment on the activity spine
userStories.description: As a user, I want a fired skill to stand out on the activity spine — the accent tick works but is easy to miss next to tool ticks; make it more legible without making the rail noisy.
acceptanceCriteria: In ActivitySpine.tsx, skill ticks get a clearly more distinct treatment than tool ticks (e.g. a larger/filled accent mark or a subtle ring) so a fired skill is legible at a glance
The prompt > skill > tool visual hierarchy and the +N density guard are preserved — the rail must stay 'graceful, not cluttered' (the F7 property); do NOT make skill ticks so loud they dominate
Hover still shows `Skill · <name>`; click still jumps to the turn
Renders correctly in light AND dark
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: a turn that fires a skill shows a clearly distinct skill tick alongside faint tool ticks
userStories.notes: Small, self-contained in ActivitySpine.tsx. Respect F7 (don't reintroduce clutter). Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Sidebar sort / group menu
userStories.description: As a user with several projects and threads, I want to sort and group the sidebar — the ↑↓ header icon should open sort/group options like t3-code.
acceptanceCriteria: The sidebar header's ↑↓ icon opens a menu with: Sort projects (last activity / created / manual), Sort threads (last activity / created), a Visible-threads count stepper, and Group projects (by repository / by path / keep separate)
Selections reorder/regroup the sidebar immediately and persist to localStorage across reloads
Defaults match current behavior: sort by last activity, group by repository
The Visible-threads count caps how many threads show per project with a 'show more' affordance beyond it
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: change the project sort and confirm the order updates and survives a reload
userStories.notes: Frontend in ChatSurface.tsx (sidebar header + grouping/sort logic). Medium. Suggested skills: automate-browser.

userStories.title: Command-palette project picker (Local folder)
userStories.description: As a user, I want adding a project to feel like a keyboard-navigable command palette (t3-code's Sources sheet), not a raw OS folder dialog.
acceptanceCriteria: The add-project flow opens a keyboard-navigable palette: ↑↓ navigate, Enter select, Backspace back (out of the folder browser), Esc close — styled as a 'Sources' sheet
V1 source is 'Local folder' (browse a folder on disk) — reuse the existing DirBrowser + /api/fs/list; remote sources (Git URL / GitHub) are explicitly OUT of scope (deferred A1-b)
Recent projects are offered inline in the palette for quick re-add
Selecting a folder creates the project exactly as today (POST /api/agent/projects) and opens a chat in it
Fully keyboard-operable end to end; a mouse still works
Typecheck passes
cd ui && npm run build passes
Verify in browser using automate-browser skill: open the picker, keyboard-navigate to Local folder, browse and select a directory, confirm the project is added
userStories.notes: Frontend; reuses DirBrowser/CwdPicker + overlay patterns. Local-folder only (A1-b remote sources deferred). Suggested skills: automate-browser.
